h1:
Where to Stay in Lopburi?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Lopburi hotels across every budget — from HOP INN's spotless rooms on the Asia Highway down to a wooden old-town guesthouse within walking distance of the train station from ฿350/night. Covering the main areas: the new town near Big C, the old town near the monkeys and temples, and the Pa Sak Jolasid dam. From roughly ฿350–900/night.
heroStats: 🏯 3 key areas (New Town·Old Town·Pa Sak Dam)
introH2: 🏯 Why does choosing the right area in Lopburi matter so much?
introHtml: Lopburi is a town where your hotel's location shapes your whole trip, because the main attractions sit in clearly separate zones — the old town (around Phra Prang Sam Yot, San Phra Kan, King Narai's Palace, and the train station) is where people come to walk among the famous monkeys, see the old temples, and arrive by train; you can sightsee on foot here without a car, but most stays are small guesthouses and resorts · the new town (Tha Sala, Khao Sam Yot, near Big C and the Narai roundabout) is the hub for malls, restaurants, and easy parking, ideal for self-drivers who want a roomy, comfortable bed in town · and the Pa Sak Jolasid dam area (Phatthana Nikhom–Chai Badan districts) sits about 50 km out of town but far closer to the dam and the sunflower fields, best for nature trips. Many people book a new-town hotel hoping to walk to the monkeys or pop over to the dam easily, then burn a day driving back and forth. This guide rounds up 12 Lopburi hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — real guest-review voices, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Lopburi has no metro; getting around relies on cars, except in the old town where you can sightsee on foot · stays in the old town (Tha Hin–Pa Tan) are often walking distance to the train station, Phra Prang Sam Yot, and the monkeys — great for train arrivals without a car, though parking is limited · new-town (Tha Sala–Khao Sam Yot) stays focus on roomy rooms, free parking, and being near Big C and restaurants, ideal for self-drivers, but it's a ~10-minute drive into the old town to see the monkeys · and the Pa Sak dam side (Phatthana Nikhom–Chai Badan) almost always requires your own car, as it's in another district ~50 km from town · the areas in this guide: Old Town — walk to monkeys, temples, train station · New Town — malls, restaurants, free parking · Pa Sak Dam — base for nature and the sunflower fields.

entries.name: HOP INN Lopburi
entries.badge: 🏆 Top score · clean rooms, one flat rate
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On the Asia Highway (Phahonyothin) · Tha Sala · near Big C
tags: 💳 One flat rate, easy to book
🛣️ On the Asia Highway, easy in/out
entries.storyHtml: HOP INN Lopburi is the highest-scoring hotel in this guide at 8.6 from 300 reviews — a budget chain whose selling point is clean, dependable rooms at one flat rate you can book without second-guessing. It sits on the Asia Highway (Phahonyothin) in Tha Sala near Big C, making in-and-out by car very easy. Real guest reviews praise the clean, tidy rooms, comfy beds, plenty of free parking, and price certainty with no haggling. The trade-offs: no pool, no restaurant, no breakfast, and roadside rooms catch some traffic noise. Best for travellers passing through Lopburi who just want a clean, comfortable room at a predictable price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room away from the main road or on a higher floor for less highway noise. No breakfast, but Big C and restaurants are nearby for a quick morning bite. It's about a 10-minute drive into the old town to see the monkeys and temples.
pros: Highest score 8.6 · clean, chain-standard rooms
One flat rate, easy to book, no price guessing
Plenty of free parking · easy highway access
Near Big C for food and shopping
cons: No pool, no restaurant, no breakfast included

entries.name: Windsor Resort Lopburi
entries.badge: 💬 Most-reviewed · walk to the train station
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old town Lopburi · Pa Tan · walk to train station, near Narai's Palace
tags: 🚉 Walk to train station, near Narai's Palace
entries.storyHtml: Windsor Resort Lopburi is the most-reviewed property in this guide — 870 reviews — and the old-town pick you can walk to the train station from, scoring 8.0. Its quirky European/Dutch-themed building is a photo magnet; it sits in the Pa Tan area, walking distance to Lopburi train station and near King Narai's Palace. Real guest reviews praise the roomy, clean rooms, free bikes for exploring the old town, free parking, and good value. The trade-offs: it's not a big resort with a pool or sleek modern rooms, some rooms catch train noise, and breakfast is fairly basic. Best for train arrivals exploring the monkey town without a car who want an affordable old-town base.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a Resort Zone room set further back for more quiet and less train noise. Borrow the free bikes to ride out to Phra Prang Sam Yot and see the monkeys in the old town. Arriving by train is the best value — you can walk over from Lopburi station.
pros: Most reviews in this guide 870 · solid data
Walk to train station, near Narai's Palace and old town
Quirky European-themed building · roomy, clean rooms
Free bikes · free parking · good value
cons: No pool, rooms aren't sleek-modern
Some rooms catch train noise · fairly basic breakfast

entries.storyHtml: The Charlotte Smart Hotel Lopburi is the freshest building in this guide — opened around 2021 — with clean, roomy rooms at a good price, scoring 8.4 from 120 reviews. It sits in the new town around Tha Sala–Khao Sam Yot, near Big C and the Narai roundabout. Real guest reviews praise the clean, new rooms, many with mountain-view balconies, free breakfast, and free private parking. The trade-offs: no pool, breakfast is basic, and it's a fair drive from the old town so you'll want a car. Best for self-drivers who want a new, clean, comfortable room in town at a budget-friendly price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a Deluxe Room with Balcony for the mountain-view balcony — the highlight of this new build. Have the free breakfast before heading out. It's about a 10-minute drive to the old town for the monkeys and temples; have a ride-hailing app ready if you don't have a car.

entries.name: JRD Grand Place Hotel
entries.badge: 🛏️ Roomy rooms with balconies · near the centre

entries.storyHtml: JRD Grand Place Hotel is a good-value in-town hotel whose selling point is roomy rooms with balconies at a budget price, scoring 8.3 from 40 reviews. It's in the Pa Tan area of new-town Lopburi near the centre, more convenient to get around than many of the Tha Sala options. Real guest reviews praise the spacious rooms, balconies in many of them, friendly service, an on-site restaurant, and free private parking. The trade-offs: no pool, a limited breakfast spread, and some decor showing its age. Best for self-drivers visiting Lopburi or here on business who want a comfortable, budget room in town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room with a balcony when booking — they feel roomier and brighter. There's an on-site restaurant but a limited breakfast spread; town restaurants are close if you want variety. Review numbers are still modest, so read across multiple sources before booking.

Near the new-town centre, easy to get around

entries.storyHtml: Lopburi Inn Resort is the only 4-star in this guide and the pick with a swimming pool — one of the largest, most convenient in-town resorts in Lopburi, scoring 7.8 from 320 reviews. It's in the new town around Tha Sala, near the easy-access Asia Highway. Real guest reviews praise the spacious rooms with balconies, the outdoor pool, gardens, banquet halls, and ample parking. The trade-offs: it's not a brand-new, design-led hotel — the building is an older-style resort — and it sits outside the old-town zone. Best for families or groups who self-drive and want a roomy room with a pool at a fair price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's one of the few Lopburi stays with a pool, so if you have kids, pick this and make the most of it. The banquet halls suit groups and events. It's about a 10-minute drive into the old town for the monkeys and temples.

entries.addr: 15-17 Phraya Kamjat Rd, Tha Hin, Mueang Lopburi
entries.storyHtml: Noom Guesthouse is the cheapest stay in this guide, from just ฿350, and the backpacker pick within walking distance of every old-town sight, scoring 8.2 from 270 reviews. It's a two-storey wooden house in the heart of the old town (Tha Hin), an easy walk to the train station, Phra Prang Sam Yot, and the monkeys. Real guest reviews praise the tasty, cheap on-site restaurant, friendly owner, and motorbike/bike rental. The trade-offs: the cheapest rooms are small and basic with thin walls that carry sound, some are fan-only, and there's no pool or large parking. Best for train arrivals who explore the old town on foot and want an affordable stay with character.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Arriving by train is the best value — walk over from Lopburi station with no extra fare. For A/C and an en-suite, ask for an A/C Double/Twin; the fan rooms are cheaper but basic. Try the on-site restaurant many reviews praise, and rent a motorbike to ride around the old town.

Walk to the train station, Phra Prang Sam Yot, and the monkeys

entries.storyHtml: Benjatara Boutique Place Resort is a good-value in-town resort whose selling point is roomy rooms, breakfast included, and free parking at a budget price, scoring 7.9 from 201 reviews. It's in the new town around Khao Sam Yot on Soi Tha Sala, near Big C and about a 10-minute drive from Phra Prang Sam Yot. Real guest reviews praise the spacious, clean rooms, cold A/C, the quiet setting, family rooms with two king beds, and convenient parking. The trade-offs: no pool, simple rooms and decor for the price, a limited breakfast selection, and Wi-Fi that's occasionally patchy. Best for self-drivers who want a comfortable room in town at a budget price that includes breakfast.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a group or family, ask for the Family Room with two king beds (~32 sqm) — roomier and better value. Open your map app before arriving, as you turn off the main road into a soi. If you need to work online, bring a mobile-data backup.

entries.storyHtml: Pasak Hillside Resort is a lakeside resort on the Chai Badan side, well suited to families or anyone wanting a nature break by the water near the Pa Sak Jolasid dam, scoring 7.8 from 164 reviews. It has spacious grounds and a quiet setting, with mountain-view rooms, wooden bungalows, and lakeside villas. Real guest reviews praise the open space, the waterside atmosphere, and the free bikes and boats. The trade-offs: it's far from old-town Lopburi (a different district, ~50 km away), some facilities are showing their age, and there's limited to do in the immediate area. Best for travellers specifically visiting the dam and sunflower fields — not those heading into town to see the monkeys.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: You'll need your own car, as it's in another district ~50 km from town. Pick a lakeside villa or bungalow for the waterside setting that's the highlight here. Try the free bikes and boats on the grounds. It's even better timed for the sunflower bloom.

entries.storyHtml: Mourakot Resort is a garden-bungalow boutique resort on the Phatthana Nikhom side, well suited to travellers visiting the Pa Sak Jolasid dam who want to stay close by in a quiet setting, scoring 8.3 from 7 reviews. Its 25 bungalows all have a balcony, with free parking and rates from around ฿700. Real guest reviews praise the quiet garden setting and the balcony on every room. To be clear about the trade-offs: no pool, no restaurant or breakfast, it's a rural zone with few shops around, and the real-review base is still very thin at just 7 reviews. Best for dam visitors who want a quiet bungalow — read across multiple sources before booking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: You'll need your own car, as it's a rural zone with few shops around. There's no restaurant or breakfast, so bring food or plan to find a spot in the district. With a thin review base, read across multiple sources and check with the property before booking.

entries.name: Lopburi Inn Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 New town Lopburi (Tha Hin) · Narai Maharat Rd · town centre
tags: 🐒 Easy to spot, with golden monkey statues out front
entries.addr: 28/9 Narai Maharat Rd, Tha Hin, Mueang Lopburi
entries.storyHtml: Lopburi Inn Hotel is an old-school, budget-friendly in-town hotel — central in the Tha Hin area, with free parking, an on-site restaurant, and easy to spot thanks to the golden monkey statues out front, scoring 6.8 from 210 reviews. It's a large ~100-room hotel on Narai Maharat Rd. Real guest reviews praise the central location, free parking, and affordable price. To be clear: a fair number of reviews flag the dated building and rooms, some with a musty smell, and there's no pool — hence the lowest score in this guide. Best for budget travellers who self-drive and just need a clean place to crash between sightseeing in the monkey town, at a price that's easy on the wallet.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Room condition varies quite a bit — ask for a better Superior room and to see it before checking in, checking the A/C, bathroom, and for any smell; staff are happy to switch. The central location is handy for food. If you weight newness and a high score heavily, look at the top-ranked options instead.

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Lopburi hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in in Lopburi?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style · the old town (Tha Hin–Pa Tan) suits those coming to walk among the monkeys, see the old temples, and arrive by train; some stays are walkable to the train station and Phra Prang Sam Yot (Noom Guesthouse, Windsor Resort), though parking is limited · the new town (Tha Sala–Khao Sam Yot) has malls, restaurants, free parking, and roomy rooms, ideal for self-drivers (HOP INN, The Charlotte, JRD, Grand Lopburi, Benjatara, Lopburi Inn Resort) · the Pa Sak dam side (Phatthana Nikhom–Chai Badan) is closer to the dam and sunflower fields than the town, best for nature trips (Pasak Hillside, Mourakot)

faq.q: ❓ How much do Lopburi hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: guesthouses and budget stays start around ฿350–650 a night (Noom Guesthouse, Phetlada, Benjatara, Windsor) · mid-range hotels and resorts up to 4-star run around ฿650–900 (The Charlotte, JRD, Grand Lopburi, Lopburi Inn Resort, Pasak Hillside, Mourakot) · all prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms; during the sunflower season and the King Narai Festival, prices run higher than usual and rooms fill fast

faq.q: ❓ Visiting Lopburi without a car to walk and see the monkeys — where should I stay?
faq.a: If you arrive by train and want to explore the old town on foot · Noom Guesthouse ฿350, a wooden house walkable to the train station, Phra Prang Sam Yot, and the monkeys, the cheapest here · Windsor Resort ฿580, a European-themed resort walkable to the station, near Narai's Palace, with free bikes and the most reviews at 870 · both are in the old town where you can reach the key sights on foot without a car

faq.q: ❓ Which Lopburi hotels have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Most Lopburi stays in this guide don't have a pool, as it's a town where stays focus on comfortable, budget-friendly rooms · the option with a pool is Lopburi Inn Resort ฿900, the only 4★ here with an outdoor pool, roomy rooms, and banquet halls, ideal for families and groups · on the Pa Sak dam side, Pasak Hillside leans on lakeside activities with free bikes and boats instead of a pool

faq.q: ❓ Using Lopburi as a base for the Pa Sak Jolasid dam — where should I stay?
faq.a: The Pa Sak Jolasid dam and sunflower fields are over in Phatthana Nikhom–Chai Badan, about 50 km from Lopburi town · if the dam is your main focus, stay on that side to cut the driving — Pasak Hillside Resort ฿900, a lakeside resort in Chai Badan, or Mourakot Resort ฿700, garden bungalows in Phatthana Nikhom · both need your own car, as they're in other districts · if you'd rather stay in town, pick a new-town hotel with free parking and drive out and back

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Lopburi hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion period, so always open all 3 and compare before booking — every review page in this guide has price-comparison links, which can save hundreds of baht a night, especially during the sunflower-bloom season and the King Narai Festival when rooms fill fast
